task: Choose a type-error break for the B3 error-path edit `f` so that the Moss check answers.
observation: A type or name error in the LEAF of the B3 DAG or fan-in (six variants: string constant, undefined name, unknown function, missing method, wrong return annotation, returned string) gave no answer from `margo --check build` within 20 s on both shapes (one variant, DAG `k = "one"`, also no answer within 300 s) (the unbroken check takes ~0.4-0.6 s). The same `+ "one"` break in the TOP node answers in 0.3-0.55 s; the time grows steeply with the break's distance from the root (DAG n005 2.2 s, n010 > 20 s; fan-in c001 2.2 s, c010 > 20 s). The cause was not investigated.
impact: An ordinary typo in a deep generic helper can look like a hang (no answer within 20 s; not proven to run forever); the error-path benchmark had to break the top node, which is the least representative place for an edit-loop error.

resolution.summary: Edit f breaks the top node; leaf breaks are recorded as ruled out. Related earlier note: probes/no_score_deep_d20_w4.moss.

task: Read the diagnostic of the B3 edit `f` failure.
observation: For `return n001_0(x) + "one"` in n000_0 the checker reports TYPE_AMBIGUOUS_OPEN_RESULT "static specialization of function 'main__root' has an unresolved result type", i.e. it names the root specialization, not the broken node or the string/Int mismatch. cargo reports E0277 "cannot add `&str` to `i64`" at the offending expression for the same text.
impact: An agent fixing the edit has to bisect the DAG instead of jumping to the cause; also a gate that compares diagnostics will see a position-free message.

task: Obtain a work counter and a correctness verdict from `cargo check` without nightly flags.
observation: `cargo check --message-format=json` exposes `fresh` on every compiler-artifact message and compiler-message objects with error code, message and spans; stderr `Checking <crate>` lines show which units rustc ran on. That was enough for a reused/rechecked counter and a structural gate with no nightly `-Z` flags. A probe showed path-crate freshness is mtime-based: touching or rewriting identical bytes rechecks the crate, a content change with the old mtime is reported fresh.
impact: Moss's own bookkeeping (margo `checked`/`skipped`, compiler counters) could offer the same structured surface; today counters need an env-var-enabled separate run and a failing check reports none.

resolution.summary: Method recorded in the README Rust comparison.

task: Measure the revert step after a failing Moss edit.
observation: After the failing edit f, the revert check (byte-identical tree) costs about 46 ms with no checker run counted, against 424-460 ms (DAG) for a full check: margo most likely answers it from the last successful interface instead of the compiler (inferred from 0 checker runs, not traced). The failing check itself reports no compiler counters.
impact: Revert-after-error is already cheap through margo's package skip; compiler-side counters do not cover failing checks, so an error-path improvement cannot be read from them.

resolution.summary: Observed; mechanism inferred from checker_runs 0, not traced.

task: Make the package fixtures survive Phase 28.6's hardened exports without changing the call graph.
observation: `export trait Scorable:` with `fn score() -> Int` in a provider package, next to untyped `export fn root(x)` generics, checks and builds under today's compiler; the consumer's plain structs with a `score()` method keep working without naming the trait, and the counters of a B1 and a fan-in fixture (21 / 168 and 55 / 440 functions / keys) are exactly the predictions. A text sweep of the fixtures flags 24 fixtures on the old sources and none on the new.
impact: Declaring the covering trait is a one-line, call-graph-neutral change in the provider, which is the kind of migration the hardening needs.

resolution.summary: Fixtures regenerated at suite 0.6.0; whether 28.6's built-in traits cover `len()` was not established, a trait was added defensively.

task: Decide how a benchmark harness isolates a content-addressed store per series.
observation: A store that defaults to ~/.cache would silently turn every 'cold' rep warm, and the only variables the harness controls are the environment and HOME. The harness therefore defines `MOSS_STORE_DIR` (plus a redirected XDG_CACHE_HOME) as the interface, scrubs inherited `MOSS_STORE*`, and gives every series a directory under the run directory; today's compiler ignores it, so the isolation is verified only against a stand-in client in selftest, not against a real store.
impact: Until the real compiler implements the variable, nothing in the harness can prove that a store-using compiler honors it; the final per-store sizes will show it (all 0 today).

resolution.summary: Contract documented in the README; needs a 28.6 implementation to confirm.
